audit.whatIsWrong: The full-layer level chart marks Fiora as the winner of all seven stages at 7/10, contradicting both the packet levelChart (Skill x5, Aatrox at first item, Fiora at 2+ items) and the content-layer whys[], which describe levels 1-5 as skill-tested and first item as Aatrox's window.
audit.why: Emerald+ win rate is 51.43% over 1153 games — a near-even lane, not a seven-stage sweep. The two layers must agree or the page contradicts itself.
audit.corrected: phases[0..4] = Skill 5/10, phases[5] = Aatrox 4/10, phases[6] = Fiora 7/10; report[2].t restated to match.

audit.why: Spikes are accurately placed: both ultimates at 6 (Grand Challenge 110/90/70s vs World Ender 120/100/80s), Aatrox's first-item bruiser window, Fiora's two-item max-HP true damage window. Mirror audit states the same shape from Aatrox's side (commit only once Riposte, 24s at rank 1, is spent).

audit.whatIsWrong: Infernal Chains (W) is only ever called 'his W chain-pull'. Its grounding — which denies Lunge (Q) as an escape — is never stated anywhere on the page, and it is the decisive interaction of the matchup.
audit.why: Fiora's entire escape pattern is Q-lunge out after a Vital proc. Aatrox's W grounds, so a landed Infernal Chains removes that exit and forces the extended trade his Deathbringer Stance and Umbral Dash healing win.
audit.corrected: Named Infernal Chains and stated the grounding in spikes[0].text and wants.foe[0]; corrected dontsFull[0].d to distinguish his bait Q1 from the two immobilizing casts that actually convert Riposte into a stun.
sources: enemyKit W flags: grounding, slow, projectile

audit.whatIsWrong: dontsFull[1] is titled 'Fight his R without anti-heal' but its body text ('Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown') is about spending an ultimate — the body does not match the heading and says nothing about anti-heal.
audit.why: Aatrox heals from three sources (Deathbringer Stance P, Umbral Dash E passive, World Ender R amp). Grievous Wounds timing is the item decision of the lane and the don't should say so.
audit.corrected: Body rewritten to name World Ender's heal amp and Executioner's Calling.

audit.why: packet.defects flags 'My Grand Challenge' in mid as a probable wrong ability name. It is a FALSE POSITIVE — Grand Challenge is Fiora's real R name per the kit. No edit made.

edits.after: His first-item bruiser spike with a live World Ender out-heals your DPS — hold until his ult is down.

edits.before: That is Aatrox's favourite window — refuse it and half his win condition is gone.
edits.after: His Q1 is bait; only his Q3 knockup and Infernal Chains convert Riposte into a stun.

edits.before: Bank Riposte for his sweetspot Q3 knockup or his W chain-pull — parry either immobilizing effect and the return becomes a STUN, freezing him so you free-proc the Vital and win the trade before his on-hit passive heal ticks.
edits.after: Bank Riposte (24s at rank 1) for his Q3 knockup or Infernal Chains — parrying either immobilizing cast turns the return into a STUN, and the chains also ground you, so Lunge is not an escape once they land. Proc the Vital instead.

edits.after: Land his Q3 knockup or Infernal Chains — the chains ground you, denying Lunge, and open the extended trade his healing wins

notes: packet.defects flags 'My Grand Challenge' as a wrong ability name — it is a false positive; Grand Challenge is Fiora's real R. No change made there. The seven-row level chart in the full layer was a straight sweep for Fiora while the content layer's whys[] described a skill-tested lane with an Aatrox first-item window; the full layer was the one out of step with the packet and the win rate, so it was flipped as an atomic group.
